answer: Operating System Fingerprinting works by analyzing the behavior of an operating system to distinguish between different types and versions. This process involves examining how the OS responds to various network protocols and requests, allowing for the identification of the specific operating system or firmware of a remote device. The technique relies on detecting unique characteristics in the implementation of protocols, which can reveal information about the operating system in use [Source 1][Source 2][Source 3].
